key_insight: Task-aware CT projection selection improves direct hemodynamic prediction under extreme sparsity, but its optimal views differ from those needed for image reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: Sparse CTA acquisition could be tailored to predict aneurysm wall shear stress rather than to maximize reconstructed image quality.
method: Generate synthetic fan-beam CTA projections from intracranial aneurysm CFD simulations.
Train a Fourier neural operator to predict spatially resolved and spatially averaged time-averaged wall shear stress.
Compare uniform and golden-angle sampling with Gumbel-Softmax, Soft top-K, and agentic AI selection across view budgets.
evidence_signal: On synthetic CFD-derived data, agentic AI and Soft top-K achieved the lowest mean spatial-field errors, with agentic AI slightly better and both substantially outperforming fixed sampling under extreme sparsity.
watch_item: Clinical generalization remains unestablished by the synthetic-data evaluation, and hemodynamics-optimized views produced poor image reconstructions.
paper_title: Agentic AI Reasoning and Learned Sampling for Task-Aware Projection Selection in Sparse-View CT: Predicting Hemodynamics
